text:
sam_sales: Kicking off ACME hybrid POC. They want Private deployment via PrivateLink + on-prem Palo Alto TLS inspect. Need architecture that either preserves client src IP or a clear SNAT fallback, firewall rules, and a quick cost sketch.

alex_solutions: Copy. Timeline? qps expectations?

sam_sales: 2-week POC, low qps initially. They have BGP to colo and can peer TGW but security prefers PrivateLink isolation.

maria_netops: FYI PrivateLink endpoints are ENIs in customer VPC; traffic from our side will SNAT to our EIP/NLB unless we build a TGW path. PrivateLink alone won't preserve original client IP through our egress.

devon_se: Two POC paths: Option A (fast): PrivateLink + static EIPs we control (customer sees our EIP as client). Option B (preserve IP): TGW + BGP announce or VPN/DirectConnect; more lead time.

jess_security: For questionnaire: KMS/HSM options, audit logs 90d, TLS cipher policy. Answer for storing customer IPs: transient only, redacted before persistent storage.

sam_sales: Pricing: any ballpark for small reserved capacity + 2 static EIPs?

alex_solutions: Ballpark reserved pool ~$6k-10k/mo depending on model; EIP costs are AWS charges + ops time. For sales use "estimate: reserved capacity + 2 static EIPs" and we'll refine.

maria_netops: Note PrivateLink/NLB connection limits. For low qps POC it's fine; call out scale caveat in docs.

sam_sales: Can we provide minimal Palo Alto allowlist for the customer?

alex_solutions: Yes. Example: allow TCP/443 from app-subnets -> interface endpoint ENIs; allow TCP/443 from our static EIP(s) if using NAT to on-prem; allow established responses; optional ICMP for health checks.

infra-bot: deploy_job:privatedeploy-poc-3312345800 started by devon_se at 3312345810  provisioning: 2x EIP placeholders + small reserved pool. ETA 03h.

sam_sales: Action items: devon -> cost sketch by EOD; alex -> firewall snippet + questionnaire draft; jess -> SOC2 attestation + incident runbook stub; maria -> confirm BGP announce feasibility in 48h window. Customer call tomorrow 09:00 PT, please have SME ready.
